a47678a.name: Gedor
a47678a.comment: the identification of Zondervan Encyclopedia of the Bible (2010) (Gedor) with "Khirbet Gadeirah, north of el-Jib" is possibly Jedireh, as it’s located just northeast. However, it’s a modern settlement, not a ruin. Khirbet Judeira, on the other hand, which International Standard Bible Encyclopedia (1979) (Gedor) mentions as a possibility, is 10km west-northwest, not north. Other sources use Gibeon (i.e., El Jib) as a reference when referring to Jedireh but don’t call it a khirbet. Demsky, Genealogy of Gibeon (1971) (page 22), from 1971, supports the identification with Jedireh ("Perhaps Judeira, 3 kilometers northeast of El-Jib"); Zondervan Encyclopedia of the Bible (2010) (Gedor)’s identification carries over unchanged from Zondervan Pictorial Encyclopedia of the Bible (1975) (Gedor); however, Zondervan Pictorial Encyclopedia of the Bible (1975) mentions both "modern Jedireh and Khirbet Gudeira," so on balance I think Zondervan Encyclopedia of the Bible (2010) (Gedor) is probably referring to Khirbet Judeira

meta.title: Biblical geography
meta.scope: Every entry in the pinned OpenBible Protestant-Bible geocoding dataset. Associations can reflect translation variants. Deuterocanonical books are outside this source's scope. Unlocated places are retained without invented coordinates.
meta.precisionNote: Points may represent a settlement, region, river or approximate area. All source candidates are preserved. Coordinates are reference points, not ancient boundary reconstructions or travel routes.
meta.scoreNote: Historical OpenBible source-weighted score (roughly through 2020); not a calibrated probability, current archaeological consensus or an endorsement. Newer findings can change assessments.
meta.modifications: Normalized verse IDs and names; flattened alternative resolutions; generated passage indices; original bibliography retained separately. Geometry and images not imported.
meta.additionalAttribution: Source coordinates marked as OpenStreetMap retain © OpenStreetMap contributors attribution and ODbL 1.0 terms.
